## A letter from all your past selves

You kept drawing, even when you lied and said you stopped. You learned to swim, late and badly and then well. You called Vó Lúcia until there was no one to call, and then you turned the calls into a book. Limonada gave you a lemon. The parrot man was real, and his name was Valdir, and Juca was right. You failed Cálculo, the driving test, and the two-year plan, and none of those were the end. You are not fearless, but you are no longer afraid of the answer. We are proud of you, and a little jealous of the window.

## A letter from all your past selves

We wrote these for you in kitchens, buses, and quiet rooms. We were scared of calculus, of the sea, of Mom's questions, of wanting too much. We hid a sketchbook under a mattress and called it a hobby. We failed, stalled on hills, and kept going. We loved Rafa and let him go. We lost Vó Lúcia and kept her laugh. We planted a lemon seed in a yogurt cup and it became a tree. We learned to float, then to swim, then to enter the water alone. We moved toward the sea, not all at once, but enough. We drew Seu Ivo and Juca and found out one name was real. We played Asa Branca badly, then fully. We are proud of you for finishing the book and for not deleting the comics in a bad mood. Keep drawing. Keep calling. Keep swimming. The window is blue. We are still here.

## Threads that kept coming back

**Limonada, the lemon tree.** Planted as three seeds in a yogurt cup labeled "MARINA" on 2014-07-09, sprouted 2014-09-21, survived frost, a move to Floripa, and ten years of overwatering. She produced her first flower in 2018-11-25 and her first lemon on 2026-01-12. The yogurt cup itself became a pencil holder. The thread runs from a yogurt cup to a balcony facing the sea.

**Seu Ivo and Juca.** The parrot man first appeared on the 7am Interbairros II on 2014-03-05. Marina named him "Seu Ivo" in her head on 2014-09-16 and the parrot "Juca" on 2014-10-19. He moved to Ponta Grossa around 2019-07. In 2025-05-24, a woman at a comics fair revealed her grandfather was Valdir, the real Seu Ivo, and the parrot really was Juca. Marina invented one name and got the other right.

**The sea dream.** First recorded 2014-07-02: standing at the edge, warm water, feet stuck. The dream changed in increments: one toe in (2015-12-14), right foot (2016-07-02), one foot (2017-07-02), both feet (2018-12-07), knees (2020-02-21), swimming (2022-07-30), floating (2023-10-23), and finally Vó Lúcia swimming beside her (2026-07-20). The calves stopped tightening. The dream kept its promise.

**Vó Lúcia and Coronel.** The grandmother in Irati, the farm dog who walked her to school. Vó told the story dozens of times, and Coronel got braver with each telling. Vó died of Covid on 2020-10-02. Marina drew 14+ pages of her stories, finished the book "Menina do Mar" on 2026-07-13, and read it aloud at Vó's grave. The laugh that "started high and fell like stairs" was the hardest thing to draw.

**Asa Branca.** Tio Beto taught three chords on 2014-04-02. The promise to learn the full song by Festa Junina became a running joke: "one more year" every year. She played it all the way through on 2023-06-24, nine years late. Tio Beto said "I told you, one more year" as if it had been one.

**Bia and the bar wall.** Names written on the wall in São Francisco on 2014-08-15, 2015-08-03, 2016-08-03, 2017-08-10, 2018-05-19, 2019-08-15. Bia moved to Floripa on 2019-08-01 and saved the spare room facing the sea. She got engaged 2025-01-24 and married 2026-05-09.

**The bus comics (Interbairros).** Started 2016-05-02, 300+ followers, Seu Ivo and Juca. Stopped in January 2017 for the factory internship. A woman at a comics fair in 2025-05-24 held a printed strip and said "this is my grandfather."

**Money checks.** From R$ 340 on the 28th in 2014 to a salary, savings fund named "MAR", and illustration paying half the bills by 2025.

**The república fridge.** Names on every yogurt, a leaky roof, a bathroom schedule as diplomatic treaty. The fridge rules survived even after Marina moved out.

**Mom and the printer.** Mom said drawing was a hobby. She printed Marina's comics on the printer Marina bought her and never said she liked them. In 2020-03-08 she texted "você desenha tão bem" for the first time.

## What you let go of

**Rafa.** The boyfriend who loved São Paulo. Broke up 2018-02-14. She kept the playlist for years, then deleted it on 2025-11-22. He married, has a daughter called Lua. She ran into him at a wedding in 2025-10-18 and danced one song in the kitchen. "Not sad. Just the pastel."

**The factory.** Started 2017-03-02, Cláudio as mentor. Quit 2023-01-15. "Being good at something you don't love is a trap." Cláudio retired. His chair stayed empty.

**The driving test.** Failed repeatedly 2017, passed 2019-04-10. The Detran hill was personal.

**The sea dream's fear.** The calves stopped tightening. The feet moved. The dream changed from standing at the edge to swimming to floating to Vó Lúcia swimming beside her.

**The sketchbook under the mattress.** Moved to the desk, then the windowsill, then the kitchen table. The hiding place became a display.

- **"Learn to swim"** (2014-03-10): Kept. 25 meters in 2022-07-19, eight years late. Dona Cida cried.

## A letter from all your past selves

Dear Marina,

We wrote this from the bus, from the república, from the factory floor, from the balcony where the sea is finally outside the window. We drew on everything: margins, napkins, receipts, fogged glass. We hid the sketchbook under the mattress and then stopped hiding it. We planted a seed in a yogurt cup and it became a tree with lemons. We failed Cálculo and passed it. We failed Asa Branca for nine years and then played it through. We were afraid of the water and then we swam.

You kept drawing. That was the one thing we all agreed on, even when we disagreed about everything else. The sea dream changed because you changed. The feet moved.

Vó Lúcia called you menina do mar. She was right. She was always right, and she would have said so, and then she would have told you to eat more.

We are proud of you. Not because you arrived, but because you kept going. The lemon tree has lemons now. You have a book. You have a window. You have us, all of us, in the margins.

— All of us, 2014–2026

## Threads that kept coming back

- **The sea dream.** From [2014-03-10] onward you stood at the edge with warm water and feet that wouldn't move, waking with tight calves. It recurred for years, then slowly shifted: one foot in [2015-12-14], both feet [2018-09-18], floating [2020-09-21], swimming [2022-01-09], and finally swimming alone at Praia Mole [2024-09-12]. - **Limonada.** A lemon seed in a yogurt cup with “MARINA” written on it [2014-07-09] became a plant, then a roommate, then a balcony tree in Floripa [2024-06-21]. She took ten years to give one ugly lemon [2026-01-12], and you treated it like a medal.
- **Vó Lúcia and Coronel.** The farm dog in Irati grew braver every time she told the story [2014-01-26; 2020-10-02; 2025-10-02]. After she died, the story became a book: *Menina do Mar* [2024-10-15; 2026-09-18].
- **Tio Beto and “Asa Branca.”** “One more year” became a family language [2014-04-07; 2023-06-24; 2026-05-09]. You finally played it through [2023-06-24], and the promise stopped being a joke.
- **Bia.** From splitting pastel de feira [2014-01-19] to saving you the room facing the sea [2024-06-21]. The wall in São Francisco faded, but the friendship did not [2015-08-15; 2024-06-21].
- **Money.** The old R$ 340 panic [2014-04-28] became a savings fund called “MAR” [2018-11-30], then “book” [2024-09-30], then a life where illustration pays half the bills [2025-12-20].
- **Swimming.** From four seconds of panic [2014-04-28] to 25 meters [2022-07-19] to swimming alone in the sea [2024-09-12]. The promise from 2014 was kept, just slowly.
- **Umbrellas.** You kept forgetting them [2014-01-05; 2014-01-09; 2018-01-08]. Curitiba never stopped being an argument with the sky.

## What you let go of

- **Rafa and São Paulo.** He bought pastéis after Cálculo failures [2015-06-08], and you broke up because you wanted different cities [2018-02-14]. Years later you ran into him at a wedding and deleted the playlist without pain [2025-10-18]. That is not failure; that is a door closing gently.
- **The factory.** It gave you Cláudio, diagrams, and a paycheck [2017-03-02], but you left in 2023 [2023-01-15]. You were good at it, and being good at something you didn’t love was the trap you named early [2017-03-15].
- **The bus comics.** *Interbairros* slept for years [2019-07-02], but Seu Ivo survived in your notebook and on strangers’ fridges [2025-05-24].
- **The república.** Four girls, one bathroom, names on yogurts [2014-02-20]. You left it, but the old wood smell stayed in your memory [2024-06-07].
- **Vó Lúcia’s Sunday calls.** They ended with her death [2020-10-02], but the habit became drawing her stories on Sundays instead [2020-11-08].

## A letter from all your past selves

Dear Marina,

We kept the sketchbook. We kept the lemon tree. We kept the sea dream, even when it scared us. We did not keep every promise on time, but we kept the important ones: drawing, swimming, calling Vó, playing the song badly until it became less bad. We let Rafa go without making him the villain. We let the factory go without pretending it was nothing. We let the bus comics rest. We did not let the sea rest. We moved toward it, slowly, with a plant in the back seat and a notebook on the passenger seat. You are not the girl who stood at the edge anymore. You are the woman who went in, came back, and drew it. That is enough. That was always enough.

Love,  
all of us, from 2014 to now.
